questions.question: Show me an example of sort_keys
Show me an example of pretty printing with sorted keys.
questions.reference: print(json.dumps({'6': 7, '4': 5}, sort_keys=True, indent=4)) prints the object over several lines with indentation and the keys sorted.

questions.question: Give me an example of compact encoding.
Show me an example of decoding JSON with a custom object_hook.
questions.reference: Define a function such as as_complex(dct) that returns complex(dct['real'], dct['imag']) for objects with '__complex__', and call json.loads(text, object_hook=as_complex).

questions.question: Show me how to use the json module from the command line.
questions.reference: Pipe JSON into python -m json, for example echo '{"json":"obj"}' | python -m json, which pretty-prints it.

questions.question: Show me an example of what happens with duplicate keys when loading JSON.
questions.reference: json.loads('{"x": 1, "x": 2, "x": 3}') returns {'x': 3}: the last value is used.

questions.question: Show the command to upgrade a package.
Show an example of saving the installed packages to a file.
questions.reference: python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt writes the installed packages to requirements.txt.

questions.question: Show the command to install all the packages listed in a requirements file.
Show an example of installing a specific version of a package.
Show an example of breaking a long expression before binary operators.
questions.reference: The correct example puts each operator at the start of the line: income = (gross_wages + taxable_interest + (dividends - qualified_dividends) - ira_deduction ...) with the operators lined up with their operands.

questions.question: Show an example of a with statement that is spread over two lines.
questions.reference: with open('/path/to/some/file/you/want/to/read') as file_1, \ open('/path/to/some/file/being/written', 'w') as file_2: file_2.write(file_1.read())
